target_customer: Couples and individuals trying to conceive who want a lower cost home alternative to clinic insemination or IVF
problem: IVF and intrauterine insemination are costly, invasive and hard to reach for many couples; the company cites over 25 million US women with limited nearby access to fertility treatment.
business_model: Direct to consumer sales of a regulated home insemination applicator, test kits and supplements
product_category: Home fertility medical device and consumer health

founders.name: Prusothman Raja
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a medical device innovator experienced in new product development and FDA processes. Met Benjamin Tee through the Stanford Biodesign program (TechCrunch 2022-05-09).

founders.name: Benjamin Tee
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a Stanford Biodesign Fellow and serial entrepreneur; the company site says the company grew from his own struggle with unexplained infertility.

competitors.name: Mosie Baby
competitors.what: At-home insemination kit with specially designed syringes, described by trade press as the first FDA cleared over the counter home insemination kit
competitors.traction_then: Ran a retrospective study of its kit in August 2020 with 350 participants targeted

technical_complexity.rationale: A silicone applicator with a proprietary surface and microenvironment design, plus a regulatory clearance; the company later lists a US device record, so the regulated device path was achieved.

defensibility.rationale: Company describes the applicator as patented and FDA cleared; simple kits like Mosie Baby are easier to copy, but clearance and clinical data take time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge. A US device listing shows the twoplus applicator in distribution and a TWOPLUS mark was registered in February 2025 per a trademark search snippet.

market_need_then: The company cites more than 25 million US women of reproductive age with limited nearby access to treatment, and TechCrunch reports it reached over a thousand households in Singapore and the UK within months of an August 2021 launch.

branding.domain_note: Consumer brand uses twoplusfertility.com while the company name is Hannah Life Technologies.

identity.voice_and_tone: Reassuring; tagline Take the stress away from trying

branding.brand_signature: Mission to help 1,000,000 couples build families
branding.community_and_virality: Company site says it has sold over 205,000 kits and links testimonials and press (self reported).

brand_strength.rationale: Empathetic positioning and a clear mission, but the consumer brand name differs from the company name and no independent press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Hannah Life, selling under the twoplus brand, launched in August 2021, reported over 300 percent quarter on quarter revenue growth, and raised a $5.15M round in May 2022 led by Monk's Hill Ventures. It remains active with a regulated applicator and a company claim of 205,000 kits sold. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, so funding after 2022 is unknown.
notes: The May 2022 round is labelled pre-Series A by TechCrunch and Monk's Hill; the schema has no such stage so it is recorded as other. The YC seed amount is not stated; TechCrunch dates it about 18 months before May 2022 and an aggregator dates it December 2020 (one aggregator claims $5.1M or $2M, unverified). Founding year conflict: YC and a Japanese outlet say 2019, another source says 2021. Mosie Baby FDA clearance date was not verified because the Fierce Biotech page returned 403; its competitor source is the August 2020 study document. Outcome search found no shutdown, layoffs or acquisition. Raja education and prior employers not found. Total raised is not stated by TechCrunch.
